request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people, claims and pools exports now use the as-of figures when an as-of date is set. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. Before the change, the main "as of exports" test failed and the other three passed.

**The cause:** the exports are built in the browser from the lists already on screen. Setting an as-of date starts a reload of the sheet as of that date. If you exported before that reload finished, the lists had just been emptied or still held today's data, so the file came out wrong. In the failing run, the people export had only its header line. Nothing on the server needed to change, since it already answers reads as of the date.

**The fix (front end only):**
- `core/session.ts`: the session now counts sheet loads that are still waiting for an answer. The parts of the screen that read data (people, settings, pools) record which load their data belongs to. A new `settled()` waits until every part it is given shows the data from the latest load.
- `people.ts`, `settings.ts`, `pools.ts`: each read records itself with the session once its data is shown.
- The three export buttons now wait for `settled()` before building the CSV. People and claims wait for the people and settings data; pools also waits for the pools data.

`settled()` checks every 20 ms, and if a read fails it gives up after 10 seconds. In that case the export uses whatever is on screen rather than hanging, so a failed reload can still give a stale file.
